title: Shortness of Breath

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Full pediatric exam for chronic disease.
rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: Respiratory symptoms — thorough lung exam. Crackles, wheezes.
rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Assess for hepatosplenomegaly, failure to thrive.
rationale.Sweat chloride test: Gold standard for CF diagnosis. >60 mEq/L = positive.
rationale.Sputum culture: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, S. aureus, H. influenzae common in CF.
rationale.Pancreatic elastase, stool: Assess pancreatic insufficiency — common in CF.
rationale.Pulmonary function tests: Obstructive pattern. FEV1 monitoring guides therapy.
rationale.Pancreatic enzyme replacement: CREON or similar — replaces digestive enzymes for malabsorption.
rationale.Fat-soluble vitamins (ADEK): Supplementation required due to fat malabsorption.
rationale.Airway clearance therapy: Chest physiotherapy, PEP valve, vest therapy.
rationale.Consult, pediatric pulmonology: CF center referral for multidisciplinary care.
rationale.Asthma diagnosis without further workup: Chronic respiratory symptoms + failure to thrive + clubbing = not typical asthma. CF must be ruled out with sweat chloride test.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a child presenting with chronic cough, recurrent respiratory infections, shortness of breath, and failure to thrive. Exam reveals nasal polyps, clubbing, and diffuse crackles. Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation in the CFTR gene on chromosome 7. The defect in chloride transport leads to thick, viscous secretions affecting the lungs, pancreas, GI tract, and reproductive system. Diagnosis is made by elevated sweat chloride test (>60 mEq/L). CXR shows hyperinflation and bronchiectasis. Management includes pancreatic enzyme replacement, fat-soluble vitamin supplementation, airway clearance techniques, and aggressive treatment of pulmonary infections.
